title: Sell Mineral Rights in Lanesboro, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Lanesboro, PA
metaDescription: Lanesboro sits in Susquehanna County, one of the most actively drilled dry-gas Marcellus counties in Pennsylvania. See what your minerals may be worth.
heroLead: Lanesboro is a historic borough on Starrucca Creek in Susquehanna County, which has been one of the busiest dry-gas Marcellus counties in the entire state for over a decade.
intro: If you had to pick one Pennsylvania county where Marcellus development never really slowed down, Susquehanna would be near the top of most lists. Operators have run steady horizontal drilling programs through this county for years, and Lanesboro sits right inside that activity, with real wells, real royalty checks, and real precedent for what a mineral interest here can be worth.

sections.heading: Why Susquehanna County Kept Its Momentum
paragraphs: The rock quality in Susquehanna County is consistently strong across the dry-gas window, and operators like Coterra have long-term development programs here rather than one-off wells. That kind of sustained activity means unit filings, permits, and production data are usually current and easy to check for a Lanesboro-area parcel.

Starrucca Creek runs right through town, and older Lanesboro-area deeds occasionally reference the creek as a boundary marker instead of a modern survey line, which is one more reason we read the original document rather than relying on a tax map alone.

sections.heading: Starrucca Creek and the Old Rail-Town Layout
paragraphs: Lanesboro's history as a rail town along Starrucca Creek left behind an odd mix of small in-town lots and larger surrounding farm tracts, each with its own mineral history. We check both types the same way, pulling the deed and confirming what was reserved versus conveyed generations ago.

sections.heading: What an Active County Means for Your Offer
paragraphs: Because Susquehanna County has so much documented drilling history, we're rarely working from guesswork on a Lanesboro parcel — there's usually a nearby unit, a nearby well, or recent royalty data to anchor an honest range.

faqs.question: Is Susquehanna County still actively being drilled?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's remained one of the more consistently active dry-gas counties in the Marcellus play, though pace shifts with gas prices.

faqs.question: Does an in-town Lanesboro lot get treated differently than farmland outside town?
faqs.answer: The evaluation process is the same, though unit geometry and access can differ — we check both carefully.

faqs.question: What operators have historically worked this area?
faqs.answer: Coterra and its predecessor Cabot Oil & Gas have been the dominant operators developing Susquehanna County for years.

faqs.question: Does Lanesboro's small size mean fewer wells nearby?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily — Susquehanna County's development has spread across large multi-tract units, so a small borough like Lanesboro can still sit inside a sizable, active unit.
